BUG: when a handler already sent an alert or set ERROR, the generic path sends a second fatal decode_error; after the handshake it is encrypted under client_handshake_key (ERROR >= KEYS_DERIVED maps to phase 1). Fix: skip when ERROR/alert already sent and record the outbound phase before entering ERROR. No nonce reuse found.

Fixed as of v3.0.0-rc2. FIXED: plaintext-path failures now send specific alerts before abort: msg_end overflow → decode_error; ServerHello state mismatch → unexpected_message; bad ServerHello content → illegal_parameter (guarded by fatal_alert_sent to avoid double-alert when tls_recv_server_hello already sent one); non-ServerHello plaintext handshake → unexpected_message; trailing bytes in record → decode_error; bad/out-of-window CCS → unexpected_message; unknown content type → unexpected_message; key derivation failure → internal_error. AEAD failures (bad_record_mac) and record-layer overflow/unexpected alerts were already present. Remaining: protocol_version is not sent as a named alert (server version mismatch rejected via illegal_parameter path).

Fixed as of v3.0.0-rc2. FIXED: ctx->keys.handshake_secret wiped by tls_secure_memzero at the end of tls_derive_application_keys (once all application-phase secrets are derived). ctx->keys.master_secret wiped immediately after resumption_master_secret derivation in tls_send_finished. Remaining keys/IVs in ctx->keys are needed for the lifetime of the connection and are wiped by tls_handshake_cleanup; stack secrets are scrubbed by tls_crypto_guard. ECDHE shared secret wiped at L4638 after use.

TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 (MUST) and TLS_AES_128_CCM_SHA256 are implemented; SHOULD-level TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 and TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256 are absent. No practical interop impact since every TLS 1.3 server supports TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256.
requirement.justification: Partial: TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256 is not intended for this platform — ChaCha20 and Poly1305 would require two entirely new primitives with no other in-tree users, for a cipher suite that no production server requires. TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 is blocked on SHA-384 support, which is low priority and may one day be added.
